transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Willowridge - Head of Platform), Priya Patel (Willowridge - CISO), Randy Cole (Compliance), Ava Martinez (Data Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking time. i'm maya from redwood, with liam our solutions engineer, we wanted to learn about your goals and constraints around data residency and compliance for LLMs.
[00:18] Jordan: thanks maya. quick intro — we are willowridge bank, medium regional bank, we run most services in eu-west and have a uk silo. exploring LLM for customer support summarization and internal docs — but compliance is the key blocker.
[00:32] Priya: hi — priya here, ciso. our ask: GDPR first, but also financial services controls, audit logs with limited retention, and we can't have raw customer PII persist in a hosted third-party system unless it's in-region and logged appropriately.
[00:47] Maya: totally, that's helpful. liam — do you want to jump in on what redwood can offer and typical patterns?
[00:52] Liam: yeah sure. at a high level redwood has three modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc or on-prem. hosted is fastest to get started, but if you need strict in-region processing and retention controls, dedicated or private are common. we support per-tenant VPC peering and customer-managed keys (kms/hsm) for private deployments.
[01:10] Randy: can you clarify kms/hsm? we need key custody in our control, ideally HSM backed. is that possible in hosted?
[01:18] Liam: good question. for hosted our standard offering uses redwood-managed KMS, but we do offer a dedicated configuration that supports customer-managed KMS in supported clouds. private deployments (VPC or on-prem) can use your HSM. hosted with bring-your-own-key is limited right now, that's a decision point.
[01:36] Priya: so hosted is risky unless we have BYOK and strict region guarantees. our legal team will want evidence that data never leaves the EU for EU customers.
[01:44] Maya: understood. one typical approach is start with hosted for low-risk eval but plan dedicated for production. liam, any notes about logging and retention?
[01:52] Liam: yes. we provide configurable logging levels — from full request/response logs (for debugging) to redacted logs (PII redaction) to no-persist mode which drops inputs after processing. retention windows are configurable for dedicated/private. hosted has default retention for 30 days but we can negotiate longer or shorter in enterprise contracts. note: the 'no-persist' mode can impact our ability to debug prompts or run analytics.
[02:17] Jordan: the no-persist mode sounds interesting but can we still get usage metrics without storing text? like token counts and errors?
[02:24] Liam: yes, telemetry like token counts, latency, errors, and anonymized usage metrics can be retained without retaining raw text. that usually satisfies ops and cost optimization needs.
[02:31] Priya: what about English vs EU residency? we need EU-only processing for EU customer data, and UK for UK customers. do you support region pinning?
[02:40] Liam: yes, region pinning is supported for dedicated/private. hosted customers can select region endpoints but some background services may route to other regions in rare failover cases — we can add contractual guarantees for dedicated.
[02:52] Randy: our compliance folks will want SOC2, ISO 27001 evidence and pen test reports. do you have those?
[02:58] Maya: we do, i'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts. we also have penetration test summaries and a security whitepaper. we'll add them to the packet.
[03:06] Ava: technical question — our app will do realtime chat for customers, we care about latency. what are tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated?
[03:13] Liam: hosted is highly optimized but multi-tenant so in bursts you may see variability. dedicated offers predictable throughput and you can tune GPU types and batch sizes. private on-prem gives you full control but adds ops overhead. cost-wise hosted is pay-as-you-go, dedicated is reserved capacity.
[03:30] Jordan: any ability to fallback? say we run dedicated but there's capacity issues, can requests fallback to hosted?
[03:36] Liam: yes — smart routing and fallback is a supported pattern. we can define policies that prefer dedicated and fallback to hosted or a smaller model variant. fallbacks can be restricted to ensure data residency — e.g., we wouldn't fallback to hosted for EU data unless contractually allowed.
[03:52] Priya: about logging again — we have a legal constraint: never log full account numbers or national ids. is PII redaction done automatically?
[04:00] Liam: we have built-in redaction heuristics and you can supply custom regex rules or use a pre-processing step client-side. many customers do client-side tokenization/PII masking before sending. we also offer a middleware that strips sensitive fields.
[04:15] Priya: client-side redaction is where we want to be, but we need assurance that server-side logs won't have residuals. what's your approach to audit logs for admin access?
[04:24] Maya: audit logs in dedicated/private can be routed to your SIEM and we support RBAC and SSO/SAML for admin access. we also maintain an access audit trail for actions on models and rollouts.
[04:36] Randy: retention windows — by default our policy is to retain logs for 1 year but we might need 7 years for some audit items. can you do long-term archival in-region?
[04:45] Liam: for dedicated/private yes, you can export logs to your own storage in-region for any retention timeframe. hosted can export to your cloud storage via connectors but there are limits and we'd want to review specifics.
[04:58] Jordan: ok procurement timeline — we aim to pick a vendor by mid april. any gotchas from your side?
[05:05] Maya: that timeline works. typical next steps: we send security docs, liam schedules tech deep dive to scope dedicated/private, ava provides sample dataset characteristics, then we'll do a benchmark/POC if needed.
[05:18] Speaker 6: quick — HIPAA? we sometimes process health-like info on auth docs, do you have HIPAA attestation?
[05:24] Liam: we don't have a HIPAA-specific certification public page right now but we have customers operating in health and we can support HIPAA with private deployments and BAAs on a case-by-case basis. we'll flag this for legal.
[05:36] Priya: encryption at rest and in transit details? also key separation — logs vs model keys?
[05:42] Liam: all traffic is TLS. at rest we encrypt with AES-256 and for dedicated/private you can supply KMS keys. logs and model keys are separated and access-controlled. HSM-backed keys are available in private setups.
[05:56] Ava: operational question — how do you handle prompt caching or KV cache? we need to ensure cached prefixes won't serve PII to other tenants.
[06:04] Liam: good point. KV cache is per-deployment/tenant and never shared across tenants. in hosted multi-tenant environments we shard caches and have isolation controls; for strict requirement you'd use dedicated/private to guarantee no cross-tenant leakage.
[06:20] Jordan: are there instances of tokenization differences causing compliance issues? like different token boundaries exposing substrings?
[06:26] Liam: tokenization is deterministic for a given model, but if you want exact-presence checks we recommend client-side normalization. we've seen customers pre-tokenize and hash sensitive fields before sending for exact compliance.
[06:40] Priya: any concerns about model fine-tuning retaining data? we won't fine-tune with PII but curious about model updates and hallucination risk exposing training data.
[06:50] Liam: by default hosted models in our catalog are not fine-tuned on customer data. if you opt into a custom model or on-prem training you'd control datasets. we also provide labeling for models that are allowed to be updated.
[07:02] Maya: to summarize, seems like options are: 1) evaluate hosted for low-risk internal only with strict redaction; 2) pilot dedicated for EU-region production with BYOK and exported logs; 3) private on-prem if legal requires it. next steps we discussed.
[07:17] Jordan: yeah that aligns. what's benchmarking look like? we want 99th p95 latency targets under 200ms for chat. is that achievable?
[07:26] Liam: with smaller context sizes and optimized kernels p95 ~150-200ms is achievable on premium GPU configs in dedicated. hosted can also hit this but depends on burst patterns. we'll plan a benchmark and share expected numbers and model variants.
[07:40] Priya: final quick question — data deletion / GDPR right to be forgotten flow. can you delete data across logs/backups?
[07:47] Liam: yes — for dedicated/private we can implement deletion workflows that remove data from primary storage and purge exported archives if requested. hosted deletion is supported but has longer timelines due to multi-tenant storage; we'll document exact SLAs.
[07:58] Randy: ok great, we'll expect the security pack. also can you share a template SOW for dedicated setup?
[08:04] Maya: yes will include SOW template and high-level pricing bands.
[08:09] Jordan: thanks all. any other questions?
[08:12] Priya: nope from me.
[08:14] Ava: none.
[08:16] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and schedule the deep dive.
[08:21] End of call.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 6 showed up), filler words and trimmed punctuation. References to model internals (kv cache, kernels) might be slightly off in terminology.
